targets.review_note: The three fractions sum to one, so mixtures are convex combinations in the first two coordinates. Parse six-decimal inputs exactly as scaled integers. Reduce requested alloys to their convex hull. Handle one raw point or a segment covering all targets explicitly. Otherwise an admissible directed raw-material edge has all target hull points on its left and the target centroid strictly on its left; minimum support is found by rotating calipers over angularly sorted directions. A shortest directed cycle bounds a polygon containing the target hull. Degenerate collinear cycles are excluded by the strict centroid check after the one/two-point cases. Bitset BFS finds the shortest cycle, hence the fewest selected raw materials. Every selected convex polygon is feasible by mixing, and any feasible selection can be replaced by its hull vertices. Independent exhaustive subset hull containment validates small cases; all arithmetic decisions are exact integers. Reset the support minimum when consecutive sorted directions have an angular gap of at least pi: walking downhill from the previous support can otherwise stop before the correct minimum. Such a gap occurs at most once per full turn, preserving the complexity.
